title: Linked List Cycle
prompt:
Return `true` if the linked list has a cycle (some node's `next` points back to an earlier node).

Do it in O(1) space with Floyd's tortoise-and-hare: a slow pointer and a fast pointer — if there's a loop, the fast one eventually laps the slow one and they meet.
hints: Fast moves 2, slow moves 1. In a cycle, the gap closes by 1 each step — they MUST meet.
Loop guard: `while (fast != null && fast.next != null)`. If fast escapes to null, there's no cycle.
Compare with `==` (same node object), and only after moving both.

solution.explanation: O(n)/O(1). This is one place where `==` is CORRECT: we're asking whether the pointers reference the same node object, not equal values. (The HashSet-of-visited-nodes solution also works but costs O(n) space.)
